media_strategy.selection_principle: LEAN media budget: prefer free data-driven charts, CSS/SVG, and interactive HTML. Exactly one generated image (hero). No video, no music, no sonification audio. Channels are chosen by what the data and the sensitive subject matter support, not a quota.

chart.reason: The dataset is fundamentally quantitative cross-state price comparisons — bar charts and ranked dot plots are the most honest, legible way to show dispersion.

image.reason: One restrained, non-identifying conceptual hero image sets a somber documentary tone without exploiting real prisoners. Budget caps generated images at one.

video.reason: LEAN budget explicitly forbids video. The story is statistical, not an event or transformation; a video would be decorative and risk exploitative or fabricated imagery of incarcerated people.

audio.reason: LEAN budget forbids generated music; no real recordings are central to the data. A tone-based sonification of prices would be decorative for this sensitive topic and add nothing the ranked charts do not already convey.

interactive_or_map.reason: A guess-first 'hours of labor' calculator lets the reader feel the wage-to-price gap before seeing it, which is far stronger than a passive chart for the piece's emotional core.

des_hero.label: Hero image — ramen and fan on a prison shelf

content.prompt: Editorial conceptual still life, no people, no text: a worn metal prison shelf holding a single packet of instant ramen and a small plastic fan under cold fluorescent light, with a faint price tag, muted desaturated greens and grays, shallow depth of field, documentary photography mood, restrained and somber, no faces, no identifying marks

des_hero.brief: Full-bleed somber still life of a single ramen packet and a small fan on a worn metal shelf under cold light. No people, no readable text. Sets a documentary, restrained tone over which the headline overlays. Dark gradient scrim at bottom for legibility.
des_hero.rationale: A conceptual object photo conveys the subject's gravity without using real images of incarcerated people, which would be exploitative for this dataset. One image only, per LEAN budget.

des_01.label: Ramen price by state — ranked bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact price per state

style.palette: single muted teal with North Carolina and Florida emphasized in a warm accent

des_01.brief: Horizontal ranked bar chart of all 46 states' cheapest ramen, sorted cheapest-to-priciest. North Carolina ($0.24, cheapest) and Florida ($1.06, priciest) are highlighted in a contrasting accent color with their values labeled directly. A subtle reference line/annotation at ~$0.32 marks the rough outside-store price. Caption notes 46 of 50 states provided data.
des_01.rationale: A full ranked bar makes the 4.4x spread undeniable as a gradient, not a cherry-picked pair. Bar over dot here because magnitude (length) reads instantly for non-experts.

des_02.label: Cross-product spread stat strip

content.label: the spread on deodorant: $0.06 in Ohio to $2.90 in Alaska

des_02.brief: A row of three large stat callouts above or beside the ramen chart: '4.4x ramen ($0.24-$1.06)', '30.6x toothpaste ($0.12-$3.67)', '48x deodorant ($0.06-$2.90)'. Big numbers, small descriptive labels. Communicates that the spread is a pattern across products, not one item.
des_02.rationale: The dispersion ratios are so striking they deserve headline-number treatment; this also surfaces ana_01's full data_table beyond just ramen.

des_03.label: Hours-of-labor calculator (guess-first interactive)

content.initial_state: Reader sees an item dropdown (default: Electric Fan) and a wage slider (default $0.06/hr, range $0.06-$0.63). A prompt asks: 'How many hours of prison work do you think this costs?' with a number input or 'I'll guess' button.
content.trigger: Reader optionally enters a guess, then clicks 'Reveal'. They can also change the item and drag the wage slider.
content.transition: A horizontal bar animates to the computed hours; the median price and the hours-of-labor are shown. Changing item/wage recomputes live (hours = median_price / wage, rounded).
content.payoff: For a fan at $0.06/hr the bar fills to 382 hours with the line 'more than nine 40-hour weeks — for one fan'. Reader feels the exchange rate viscerally.

des_03.brief: Inline vanilla-JS widget. Dropdown of the 9 items in ana_03's data_table; wage slider 0.06-0.63. Live computes hours = median_price / wage. Animated bar + big hours number. Pre-reveal it invites a guess to maximize the surprise of 382 hours. All numbers come from ana_03's data_table (median_price); hours recomputed client-side from the slider. Include a small note that wages are from external reporting (det_02).
des_03.rationale: The wage-to-price gap is the emotional spine; letting readers guess and then drag the wage makes them discover how brutal the math is rather than read it passively. Chosen over a static chart per the interactive-preference rule for surprising findings.

des_04.label: Hours-per-item companion bar chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing median price and hours at both $0.06 and $0.25

style.log_or_break_note: Electric Fan (382h) dwarfs others; consider a broken/annotated scale or label the fan value directly so the small items remain readable

des_04.brief: Horizontal bar chart, hours of labor at $0.06/hr per item, sorted descending. Electric Fan (382h) highlighted. Because the fan dwarfs the rest, label the fan bar's value directly and keep the axis honest; smaller items (ramen 8h, toothpaste 21h) must remain readable. Tooltip shows both wage scenarios.
des_04.rationale: Pairs the interactive with a fixed reference view so the reader can compare all items at the lowest wage at a glance.

des_05.label: Electric fan price by state — ranked dot/bar

style.palette: cool blue with Nevada (high) and Wyoming (low) emphasized

des_05.brief: Horizontal ranked bar of cheapest fan price across all 30 states that list one, priciest at top. Nevada ($43.80) and Wyoming ($10.02) emphasized. A reference annotation can note the 4.4x spread. Keep state labels legible.
des_05.rationale: Mirrors the ramen chart's form deliberately to show the same 4.4x spread recurs on a health-critical item, reinforcing the thesis through visual rhyme.

des_06.label: Price by product type — religion vs staples

content.color: category (Religious / Comfort / Food / Hygiene) — color-code so the religious items at the top stand out
content.interaction: hover tooltip with median price and number of states

style.palette: categorical: religious items in one accent, staples muted

des_06.brief: Horizontal bar of all 23 product types by median price, descending. Color bars by an inferred category so the cluster of religious items + the fan at the top is visually distinct from the cheap staples (toothbrush, ramen, soap) at the bottom. Programmer assigns category by product name: Crucifix/Quran/Star of David/Prayer Rug/Hijab/Kufi Cap/Bible/Islamic Prayer Beads/Yarmulke/Rosary Beads = Religious; Electric Fan/Reading Glasses/Relaxer = Comfort/Health; Peanut Butter/Mac and Cheese/Beans/Ramen = Food; rest = Hygiene. Annotate the Quran vs Bible gap. Caption acknowledges small samples for some religious items.
des_06.rationale: A single ranked, category-colored bar makes the moral turn land: the costliest goods are faith items and a fan; the cheapest are the things a prison cannot withhold.

des_07.label: Quran vs Bible stat callout

content.label: median price of a Quran versus a Bible — nearly 5x more for the central text of Islam

des_07.brief: A two-number stat callout contrasting Quran median ($25.99) and Bible median ($5.21), with the ~5x framing. Placed within edt_04 near the religion chart.
des_07.rationale: The single most quotable disparity in the piece deserves headline treatment.

des_08.label: Vendor share — who runs the store

style.palette: muted; private vendors in one tone, State-run in another

des_08.brief: Horizontal bar of vendors by number of states served. State-run (17) and Keefe Commissary (16) dominate; the long tail of single-state vendors shown below. Color private vendors distinctly from State-run to support the kickback point in the prose.
des_08.rationale: Shows concentration of the captive market in a few private operators, grounding the 'who profits' close.

des_09.label: Cheapest vs priciest states — diverging bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip with mean price per item

style.palette: two-tone: priciest in warm, cheapest in cool

des_09.brief: Horizontal bar of the 8 priciest and 8 cheapest states by mean cheapest-price-per-item, two-tone by rank_group. Indiana ($8.36) at top and Michigan ($0.93) at bottom emphasized, with the ~9x framing annotated. This is the closing 'geography of cost' visual.
des_09.rationale: Ends the piece on the central thesis made spatial: the same basket of needs costs ~9x more depending on the state.

page_rhythm.tone: dark, somber editorial — restrained, documentary, data-forward
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-first within each section, with one decisive visual or interactive directly below the prose; charts deliberately rhyme in form (ramen ranked bar, fan ranked bar) to reinforce the recurring 4.4x spread
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: No audio card, no video, no map. The emotional centerpiece is a guess-first labor calculator, not a hero chart. Charts use a consistent muted palette with sparing warm accents only on the two endpoints that carry the argument, avoiding rainbow dashboards. Exactly one generated image keeps the page from feeling like stock-photo journalism.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Large stat callouts (~64px) for the dispersion ratios and the Quran/Bible contrast; serif body (Georgia) for narrative gravity, system-ui for chart/UI labels; thin section dividers; pull the key numbers ($0.24/$1.06, 382 hours, $25.99 vs $5.21) into emphasized inline spans.
